what: SQM mines the Atacama desert in Chile. It pumps brine to extract lithium for batteries, and also produces iodine, potassium nitrate fertilisers and solar salts.
customers: Battery and electric vehicle makers buying lithium, plus farmers and pharmaceutical companies for the other products.
money: lithium carbonate and hydroxide from Atacama brine
used in X-ray contrast media and electronics
moat: The Atacama brine is the cheapest lithium resource on earth: evaporating it in the desert costs a fraction of mining hard rock, which keeps SQM profitable at prices that shut other producers down.
risks: Lithium prices collapsed from the 2022 peak, taking revenue from $10.7B to $4.6B
The Chilean state, through Codelco, is taking a controlling role in the Atacama operation from 2025
$6.1B of debt in a business whose revenue can halve in a year
opportunities: 7.8 times earnings and 3.9 times EBITDA, with $2.5B of free cash flow
Analysts see about 62% upside, with 18 covering the stock
Iodine prices are at records and that business is steady regardless of lithium
watch: Lithium prices and volumes, and the terms of the Codelco partnership.
